cards.title: Help at every level of the command tree, plus a version flag
cards.user_does: Runs kolux with no arguments, adds --help to any group or command, types kolux help followed by a command path, or runs kolux --version.
cards.user_sees: With no arguments or at the root, a sectioned overview: command groups by purpose, common commands, the selector grammar, option groups, behaviour notes and examples. A group lists its commands with one-line purposes. A command shows its usage line, purpose, every option with a short description, notes and examples. --version prints the build version alone.
rules: Help never needs the app running and never builds a runtime connection.
A help path that names no command and no group prints the nearest help plus a suggestion and exits 1; a valid group or command exits 0.
Every command lists the four global options (help, json, pairing code, environment).
Hidden compatibility commands (deprecated terminal stop, the tmux shim) are never shown in help or suggestions.
Root help names the canonical close command, not the deprecated stop.

Every non-hidden command must be reachable from its group help, even ones the root overview leaves out (worktree changes and overlap, agent hooks, claude-teams, orchestration request-show and many browser verbs).
Bundled skill guides may only mention command paths and flags the CLI actually defines (parity check over guides and references).
--version or -v counts only when it is the sole argument; if the version cannot be determined it prints a reason on stderr and exits 1.
acceptance: With the app closed, kolux --help prints the overview and exits 0 without any not-running message.
kolux worktree --help lists list, show, current, create, set, rm, ps, changes and overlap.
kolux help terminal sned prints help, offers terminal send, exits 1.
kolux --version prints one version line; kolux --version --json is treated as a normal command parse, not a version print.
cards.compat: Words: help, --help, --version, -v. Help is reachable as `kolux help <path>` and `<path> --help`.

cards.title: Argument grammar: flags, values, aliases and positionals
cards.user_does: Types a command with flags in any order, using space-separated or equals-joined values, aliases, or a trailing positional argument.
cards.user_sees: The command runs with the values exactly as typed; aliases behave exactly like the canonical command; missing or malformed values are rejected with a message naming the flag.
rules: Both --flag value and --flag=value work; the equals form splits on the first equals sign so values may contain more.
--flag= is an explicit empty string, and empty values are kept where they are meaningful (cookie value, storage value, credential password).
A value that itself starts with -- can only be passed with the equals form.
Boolean and value flags may sit between command words; an unknown flag never swallows the next command word.
A selector value that happens to equal a command or group name is kept as a value.
Repeatable flags (skills install --skill) accumulate; ordinary string flags keep a single value.

Aliases resolve to the canonical command before dispatch: worktree remove and worktree delete to rm, terminal focus to switch, skills show to get, orchestration run to coordinator-start, orchestration run-stop to coordinator-stop.

Positional arguments (file path for file open, skill name for skills get, automation id for edit/remove/run/show) bind after alias resolution; passing the same id both positionally and by flag with different values is rejected.
Global flags (help, json, pairing code, environment) are accepted on every command even when its spec omits them.
Flags that need a value fail when given none or an empty one (for example --worktree, --mode, --agent, --retry-request, --wait-submit).
Verb policy: deletion commands use rm (other verbs only as aliases), single-item reads use show (get only where grandfathered).
Global flags may come before the command words; a bare -- in front of the command is skipped, and a value that looks like a command word stays a value.
acceptance: kolux cookie set --name a --value= sends an empty value; omitting --value is rejected before any app call.
kolux worktree delete --worktree name:x runs the same code path as worktree rm.
kolux skills install --skill a --skill b installs both.
kolux file open --worktree with no value fails before any cwd lookup or app call.
cards.compat: Flag syntax: --flag value, --flag=value, --flag= (empty). Aliases listed in rules are part of the interface.

cards.title: Typos are caught before contacting the app, with safe did-you-mean suggestions
cards.user_does: Mistypes a command word or flag.
cards.user_sees: An error naming the unknown word, the closest valid command or flag as a next step, and for flags the list of flags that command accepts. Exit code is nonzero.
rules: Command and flag validation happens before any runtime lookup, so a typo never produces a misleading not-running error.
Suggestions consider only commands at the same depth (group names for a bad group, verbs for a bad verb) and include alias paths.
Suggestions allow up to three edits; very long tokens skip distance work entirely but still list valid flags.
A benign typo is never steered to a destructive command; a destructive suggestion (rm, delete, close or anything flagged destructive) needs a one-edit near miss of a destructive word.
Hidden compatibility commands are never suggested.
Where a flag was renamed on one verb (caller handle moved from --from to --terminal), the error points to the new flag only on that verb.
In --json mode the suggestion is carried as structured next steps in the error data.

A mistyped flag placed before or between the command words (for example a misspelt global flag in front of the group) is reported as an unknown flag on the full command path, before the app is contacted.
acceptance: kolux worktre list suggests worktree list and exits nonzero with the app closed.
kolux worktree rmm suggests rm; kolux worktree lst never suggests rm.
kolux terminal list --worktre suggests --worktree and lists accepted flags.
kolux --jso worktree --json list exits 1 naming the unknown flag and the worktree list command, with no app call.

cards.title: --json output and structured errors
cards.user_does: Adds --json to any command, typically from a script or an agent.
cards.user_sees: Success prints the whole response envelope as indented JSON on stdout (request id, ok true, result, metadata). Failure prints an envelope with ok false and an error carrying a code, a message and recovery data. Without --json, results print as readable text and errors go to stderr with next-step lines.
rules: Errors raised inside the CLI itself use a local request id and a null runtime id in the failure envelope.
The failure envelope keeps recovery data: selector grammar for a bad worktree selector, did-you-mean steps, mutation-recovery commands, automation owner-conflict steps.
Error-specific recovery wins over generic hints; mutation recovery is never replaced by generic startup advice.
When the runtime is unreachable, text mode appends advice to run kolux open first (except for orchestration mutations that already carry their own recovery).
Interactive login prompts never write into the JSON stdout stream.
Responses are validated: malformed frames and responses whose id does not match the request are rejected; long waits emit keepalive frames that are not mistaken for results.
Base64 payloads report decoded byte size rather than raw string length.
Exit code is 1 on failure in both modes.
Next-step commands printed in errors and receipts quote values that contain spaces for the current shell so they paste as is; simple selectors stay unquoted.
acceptance: kolux worktree show --worktree 123 --json with a bare id prints ok false, a selector error code and the valid selector forms in data.
kolux status --json with the app closed prints a parseable envelope.
kolux account add --json keeps login prompts off stdout so the output still parses.
cards.compat: Envelope fields: id, ok, result, error{code,message,data}, _meta{runtimeId}. Text errors on stderr, JSON on stdout.

cards.title: Exit codes
cards.user_does: Runs kolux from a script or agent and checks the exit status.
cards.user_sees: 0 on success and 1 on any error; a small number of commands use other codes for specific hand-offs.
rules: 1: validation errors, unknown help paths, unreachable app, runtime failures, failed or unknown orchestration worker receipts.
2: the Windows kolux.cmd shim refusing orchestration send or reply.
75: orchestration ask on the packaged Windows legacy protocol hands the wait back to the caller; resuming the same question does not hand off again.
terminal wait exits nonzero when the wait ends blocked without the condition being met.
skills install and update forward the exit code of the package tool they run.
claude-teams and the hidden tmux shim return the code of what they forwarded to.
kolux.cmd returns the launcher's own exit code, and 1 when the launcher binary is missing.
acceptance: A bad flag exits 1; a successful kolux status exits 0.
kolux.cmd orchestration send exits 2 with a pointer to kolux.exe.
kolux terminal wait --for exit --timeout-ms 1 on a running process exits nonzero.
cards.compat: Exit codes 0, 1, 2 (cmd shim refusal), 75 (Windows ask hand-off).

cards.title: Windows: kolux.cmd shim versus kolux.exe launcher
cards.user_does: Calls kolux on Windows from cmd, PowerShell or an agent, sometimes with multi-line message bodies.
cards.user_sees: kolux.cmd forwards everything to kolux.exe next to it and returns its exit code; for orchestration send and reply it refuses with a message to use kolux.exe instead.
rules: The shim looks for the launcher in its own folder; if missing it prints an error on stderr and exits 1.
orchestration send and reply are refused (exit 2) because cmd re-parses arguments and could execute or cut off embedded newlines in a message body.
kolux.exe forwards multi-line bodies unchanged.
The shipped CLI lives under the per-user install folder resources/bin; the shell command name is kolux.cmd on Windows.
Group addresses such as @all must be quoted in PowerShell.
Values that PowerShell 5.1 strips quotes from (JSON passed to a flag) are detected and reported instead of silently misparsed; the native argv boundary recovers dependency lists.
acceptance: kolux.cmd status forwards and exits with the launcher's code.
kolux.cmd orchestration reply --id x --body y exits 2 without sending.
kolux.exe orchestration send with a two-line body delivers both lines intact.
cards.compat: Executable names kolux.cmd and kolux.exe; shim refusal exit 2.

cards.title: kolux works inside every Kolux terminal without setup
cards.user_does: Runs kolux (or an agent does) in any terminal pane Kolux opened.
cards.user_sees: The command resolves to the CLI bundled with the running Kolux version, even if it was never registered on the system PATH.
rules: Kolux puts its bundled CLI folder first on the PATH of every child terminal so the version always matches the app.
On Linux a terminal shim folder provides the bare kolux name inside Kolux terminals.
Agents in Kolux terminals also receive their own terminal handle and pane key in the environment so orchestration commands know who is calling.
acceptance: Open a new pane on a machine with no system registration: kolux status succeeds.
With an older kolux registered on the system PATH, kolux --version in a Kolux pane prints the app's own version.
cards.compat: Environment variables KOLUX_TERMINAL_HANDLE and KOLUX_PANE_KEY are set in Kolux terminals.

cards.title: Register or remove the kolux command on the system PATH
cards.user_does: Uses the CLI section in Settings to register kolux for terminals outside Kolux, or to remove it.
cards.user_sees: The section says where the command will be registered for this OS, shows whether it is registered, and offers register or remove; failures name the path in the way and how to fix it. It also offers to install the matching kolux agent skill.
rules: Windows: adds the CLI folder to the user PATH in the registry, case-insensitive about the variable name; if the PATH state cannot be read it shows an unknown state and offers no change.
macOS: a link in /usr/local/bin, with an elevated-permission fallback when the folder is not writable.
Linux: a launcher in ~/.local/bin, with a warning when that folder is not on PATH; AppImage installs get a stable launcher that survives moving or updating the AppImage.
Development builds register a separate kolux-dev command so they never replace the installed one.
An unknown file or link already at the target is reported as a conflict and left alone; stale launchers Kolux itself wrote are replaced; legacy wrappers are cleaned up.
A failed or partial registration never shows a success message.
Register and remove re-check the target after any elevated step: a file or link someone else put there meanwhile is put back, never deleted, and a slow elevated step reports its timeout as an error.

AppImage installs: the stable launcher keeps answering while a newer version is published and picks it up once it appears, works on file systems without hard links, and older extracted copies are cleaned up after a grace period without touching other installs.
Windows: removing an entry that is not on the user PATH changes nothing.
acceptance: Register on Windows, open a new external terminal: kolux --version works.
Put an unrelated file at the macOS target path: register reports the conflict with the path and leaves the file untouched.
Remove: the command no longer resolves in a new external terminal.
cards.compat: Command names kolux (and kolux-dev for development builds); install locations per OS.

cards.title: Selectors for repos, worktrees and terminals, inferred from the current folder
cards.user_does: Names a repo, worktree or terminal on a command, or leaves it out and runs from inside a worktree folder.
cards.user_sees: Commands act on the named target; when omitted, many commands act on the worktree that contains the current folder. A bad selector fails with the valid forms listed.
rules: Repo selectors: id:, name:, path:.
Worktree selectors: identity:, id:<repo-id>::<path>, name:, branch:, issue:, path:, and active or current for the worktree enclosing the current folder.
Parent-worktree selectors additionally accept folder:<id> and worktree:<id>.
Terminal handles are issued by the app (from terminal list) and are the preferred way to address a terminal repeatedly.
A bare id with no prefix is rejected with a message naming the value and the accepted forms, in text and JSON.
Ambiguous names never resolve silently.
WSL shells: a path under a shared /mnt drive resolves without needing the caller's distro; when two distros spell the same path, the caller's distro wins.
acceptance: From inside a worktree folder, kolux worktree current shows that worktree.
kolux worktree show --worktree 42 fails and lists the selector forms.
Two worktrees named alike: name: selector fails as ambiguous instead of picking one.
cards.compat: Selector prefixes listed in rules are part of the interface.

cards.title: Which commands need the app running
cards.user_does: Runs a kolux command while the app may or may not be open.
cards.user_sees: Most commands talk to the running app and, if it is not reachable, fail with advice to run kolux open first. A few commands answer locally with the app closed.
rules: Local answers without the app: help, --version, agent-context, skills list, skills get, skills install/update (they run a package tool), agent hooks commands that edit local settings.
The runtime connection is created lazily: help and validation errors never load or contact it, and one connection is reused for the whole command.
A runtime too old for a command is named as a version gap rather than a generic failure.
A generic runtime timeout is not reported as the app being down.
acceptance: Close the app: kolux agent-context --json and kolux skills list succeed; kolux terminal list fails with the run-open advice.
kolux --help with the app closed returns promptly.

cards.title: kolux open
cards.user_does: Runs kolux open.
cards.user_sees: Kolux starts, or the already-running window comes to the front; the command returns once the app can answer CLI calls.
rules: Activates the window even when the app is already reachable.
If only a background server is running, waits for it to show a desktop window; fails clearly if that server cannot become the desktop app safely.
Times out with an error if the app never answers.
acceptance: App closed: kolux open launches it and exits 0 once ready.
App minimised: kolux open brings it forward.
cards.compat: Command word: open.

cards.title: kolux status
cards.user_does: Runs kolux status.
cards.user_sees: Whether the app is running and ready, not running, left stale (startup files exist but nothing answers), or reachable but still loading its workspace graph.
rules: States: running, not running, stale bootstrap, graph not ready.
Works and reports cleanly when the app is closed; --json gives the same state machine-readably.
acceptance: App closed: reports not running.
Kill the app hard leaving its files: reports stale.
App up: reports running.
cards.compat: Command word: status; state names in --json output.

cards.title: kolux claude-teams: run Claude Code agent teams in Kolux panes
cards.user_does: Runs kolux claude-teams followed by any Claude Code arguments.
cards.user_sees: Claude Code starts with team members appearing as Kolux panes; on Windows the command says native team panes are not supported.
rules: Everything after claude-teams is passed to Claude Code untouched, so new Claude flags work without Kolux changes.
The Claude child gets the caller's environment but never the Electron run-as-node switch.
A hidden tmux-compatible shim answers Claude's pane commands through the app and returns their output and exit code; it is never listed in help.
acceptance: kolux claude-teams --some-new-flag reaches Claude unchanged.
On Windows the command explains it is unsupported.
cards.compat: Command word claude-teams with raw passthrough arguments.

cards.title: kolux account add and list
cards.user_does: Runs kolux account add (optionally choosing the provider) to sign in another account, or account list to see them.
cards.user_sees: add runs the provider's own login in the terminal and registers the result as a Kolux account; list shows registered accounts with the active one marked.
rules: Provider defaults to Claude when --agent is omitted; an empty --agent is rejected rather than defaulting.
Codex sign-in uses device authorisation.
Fails before starting a login if the app is not reachable or too old to import accounts.
Interrupting the login (Ctrl+C, closed SSH session) cleans up the temporary credentials and restores the previous macOS Keychain entry; a second interrupt waits for cleanup.
A successful sign-in still fails if temporary credentials cannot be removed afterwards.
list does not force a usage refresh from providers.
Always runs on this machine; remote-target flags are ignored.
acceptance: kolux account add completes a Claude login and the account appears in kolux account list.
Ctrl+C mid-login leaves no stray credentials.
cards.compat: Commands account add [--agent claude|codex|...], account list.

cards.title: kolux repo: list, add, show, base ref and ref search
cards.user_does: Lists repos, adds a folder as a repo, shows one, sets its default base ref, or searches its refs.
cards.user_sees: Repo rows with ids usable in selectors; add registers the folder; set-base-ref changes the default base for new worktrees; search-refs lists matching branches and tags.
rules: repo add resolves a relative path against the folder the command was run from.
Repo selectors use id:, name: or path:.
search-refs takes --query and --limit; repo selection follows the repo selector rules.
acceptance: From a git folder, kolux repo add --path . registers it and repo list shows it.
kolux repo set-base-ref then worktree create without --base-branch uses the new base.
cards.compat: Commands repo list|add|show|set-base-ref|search-refs.

cards.title: kolux project list
cards.user_does: Runs kolux project list.
cards.user_sees: The durable projects Kolux knows about.
rules: Reads through the project-first listing; host filtering belongs to the dropped host-setup feature.
acceptance: kolux project list --json returns every project shown in the app.
cards.compat: Command project list.

cards.title: kolux worktree list, show, current and ps
cards.user_does: Lists worktrees (optionally for one repo, with a row limit), shows one, asks which worktree the current folder is in, or lists live sessions across worktrees.
cards.user_sees: Worktree rows with selectors, branch, parent and child lineage and status; current names the enclosing worktree; ps lists running sessions per worktree.
rules: Listings state which hosts they cover and which were omitted, so an empty result is never read as absolute.
current is resolved from the current folder only for the local app.
--limit caps rows.
acceptance: kolux worktree list --repo name:x lists only that repo's worktrees.
kolux worktree current inside a worktree prints it; outside any worktree it fails with a selector hint.
cards.compat: Commands worktree list|show|current|ps.

cards.title: kolux worktree create, optionally launching an agent in it
cards.user_does: Runs kolux worktree create with a name, optional repo, base branch, agent, prompt, issue, comment and setup policy.
cards.user_sees: A new isolated checkout appears in Kolux; with --agent its first terminal starts that agent (with the prompt if given). It is created in the background unless --activate asks to reveal it.
rules: Repo is inferred from the current folder's worktree when --repo is omitted.
--agent must be a known agent; --prompt without --agent is rejected; empty values for agent, prompt or setup are rejected.
--setup run, skip or inherit controls the repo's setup hooks; contradictory setup flags are rejected; --run-hooks opts into setup and activation.
--base-branch defaults to the repo's default base.

Lineage: the new worktree's parent is inferred from the calling worktree unless --parent-worktree names one or --no-parent is given; a bare --parent-worktree is rejected; the removed parent-workspace flag is rejected; contradictory parent flags fail before any selector is resolved.
--no-parent affects only Kolux lineage, not which branch the checkout starts from.
The caller's terminal handle is recorded, and every CLI-created worktree is marked as CLI-created even from an outside shell.
--issue links a GitHub issue number.
When called from a terminal of a plain folder workspace, that folder workspace is recorded as the new worktree's parent.
acceptance: From inside worktree A, kolux worktree create --name b --agent claude --prompt hi makes b with parent A, starts Claude in its first terminal, and does not steal focus.
Same with --activate reveals b.
kolux worktree create --name b --prompt hi fails: prompt needs agent.
cards.compat: Command worktree create and flags --repo --name --agent --prompt --base-branch --issue --comment --setup --parent-worktree --no-parent --run-hooks --activate.

cards.title: kolux worktree set: rename, link, comment, board status and lineage
cards.user_does: Runs kolux worktree set on a worktree with a new display name, issue, comment, board status or parent.
cards.user_sees: The worktree's card in Kolux updates accordingly.
rules: --workspace-status takes a board status id; built-in ids are todo, in-progress, in-review and completed.
--issue null clears the linked issue.
Parent can be set, resolved from current, or removed with --no-parent; contradictory or bare parent flags are rejected before lookup.
active as the selector means the worktree of the current folder.
acceptance: kolux worktree set --worktree active --workspace-status in-review moves the card to In review.
kolux worktree set --worktree active --issue null removes the issue link.
cards.compat: Command worktree set; flags --display-name --issue --comment --workspace-status --parent-worktree --no-parent.

cards.title: kolux worktree rm (alias remove, delete)
cards.user_does: Runs kolux worktree rm on a worktree, optionally with --force or --run-hooks.
cards.user_sees: The worktree is removed from disk and from Kolux.
rules: Marked destructive: typo suggestions never lead here from benign words.
--force forces the checkout removal only; it never forces deleting the branch.
--run-hooks runs the repo's archive hooks.
acceptance: kolux worktree delete --worktree name:x behaves exactly like rm.
With uncommitted changes rm fails; with --force it removes the checkout and keeps the branch.
cards.compat: Command worktree rm with aliases worktree remove and worktree delete; flags --force --run-hooks.

cards.title: kolux worktree changes and overlap: what a worktree touched and who else touches it
cards.user_does: Runs kolux worktree changes or worktree overlap, by default for the current worktree.
cards.user_sees: changes lists files changed against the base (committed and uncommitted together). overlap lists sibling worktrees that touch the same files and predicts whether their committed work would conflict.
rules: Both are read-only and default to the current folder's worktree.
changes reports a null base when the base cannot be resolved; a plain folder workspace reports unsupported.
overlap stays within the same repo, including hidden worktrees.
Conflict prediction uses the committed tips; when it cannot be checked (old Git, remote, failure) it says unverifiable, never clean.
The text output says it could not verify instead of claiming no siblings when the scan was not authoritative, and flags siblings whose own change list failed.
acceptance: Two worktrees editing the same file: overlap lists that file and the sibling.
Force the merge check to fail: overlap prints unverifiable, not clean.
cards.compat: Commands worktree changes and worktree overlap.

cards.title: kolux file open, diff and open-changed
cards.user_does: Opens a file in the Kolux editor, opens a diff for a file, or opens every changed file of a worktree.
cards.user_sees: The files or diffs open in the app; the command reports which were opened and which were skipped.
rules: A relative path opens in the worktree of the current folder; an explicit --worktree skips folder inference.
open-changed opens diffs by default and can also open edit tabs; deleted files are skipped for editing; unresolved conflicts are skipped in diff mode.
Diffs the app could not open are reported as skipped, not opened.
--mode is validated before any lookup.

An absolute path that lies inside the target worktree is accepted and opened as that worktree's relative path (also when a WSL shell spells a Windows worktree path the Linux way); the worktree root itself is rejected as a folder, not a file to open.
file diff --staged opens the staged changes instead of the working-tree changes; the path can be positional or --path.
acceptance: kolux file open src/a.ts inside a worktree opens that file.
kolux file open-changed with a deleted file lists it under skipped.
kolux file open with an absolute path inside the current worktree opens that file; naming the worktree root itself exits 1 without opening anything.
cards.compat: Commands file open|diff|open-changed; flags --worktree --mode.

cards.title: kolux terminal list and show
cards.user_does: Lists terminals (optionally for one worktree, with a limit) or shows one by handle.
cards.user_sees: Terminal rows with handles, titles, worktree and the host each runs on; the readable listing also draws tabs, split groups and nested panes.
rules: Tab and pane layout is included in the readable listing; JSON callers get it only with --include-visual-layouts.
The listing states covered and omitted hosts; a row whose host is unknown says unverifiable rather than local.
An empty listing still says what scope it covered.
acceptance: kolux terminal list --json returns handles usable with terminal read and send.
kolux terminal list shows split panes nested under their tab.
cards.compat: Commands terminal list|show; flags --worktree --limit --include-visual-layouts --terminal.

cards.title: kolux terminal read: output history or the current screen
cards.user_does: Reads a terminal's output by handle, paging with a cursor, or asks for the rendered screen.
cards.user_sees: Recent output lines with a cursor for the next read, or the current visible frame with --screen.
rules: --cursor returns only output after that point; --limit caps lines.
When only part of the output was retained the result warns and says how to continue from the oldest cursor.
--screen and --cursor cannot be combined, because a screen has no history.
If a screen was asked for but only the stream exists, it warns; an older host's stream is never passed off as a screen.
Text the user has typed but not sent in an agent's input box is labelled separately from terminal output.
acceptance: kolux terminal read --terminal h --screen returns the visible frame.
kolux terminal read --terminal h --screen --cursor 5 is rejected.
cards.compat: Command terminal read; flags --terminal --cursor --limit --screen.

cards.title: kolux terminal send and wait
cards.user_does: Types text into a terminal (optionally pressing Enter or sending an interrupt), or waits for a terminal to exit or for its agent to go idle.
cards.user_sees: send returns a receipt saying what was delivered and, for prompts to an agent, whether the agent accepted and started the turn. wait returns when the condition is met or the timeout passes.
rules: Text plus Enter to an agent is treated as a prompt: the receipt reports the delivery observation and warns if Enter appeared to be swallowed.
Text alone or a bare Enter is plain input.
--wait-submit only watches for the accepted prompt for the given time; on timeout it returns the queued receipt and never re-sends.
--retry-request takes a request id for exact retry after an unknown result; older hosts refuse the retry before sending anything and are never reported as having submitted.
If a structured chat session blocked the send, the error explains how to recover.
When a supported send never reached turn start, the result names the next command to run.
wait --for takes exit or tui-idle, with --timeout-ms; an unsatisfied blocked result exits nonzero.
acceptance: kolux terminal send --terminal h --text hi --enter to an idle Claude pane returns a receipt showing the turn started.
kolux terminal wait --terminal h --for tui-idle returns after the agent finishes.
cards.compat: Commands terminal send|wait; flags --terminal --text --enter --interrupt --wait-submit --retry-request --for exit|tui-idle --timeout-ms.

cards.title: kolux terminal create, split, rename and switch (alias focus)
cards.user_does: Opens a new terminal in a worktree with an optional startup command and title, splits an existing one, renames one, or brings one into view.
cards.user_sees: The terminal appears in the worktree's tabs; it is revealed only when asked.
rules: create resolves the worktree from the current folder when active is given or nothing is named.
Interactive Claude or Codex startup commands start in the background unless --focus is given; one-shot forms (exec, print, review, help) are not forced onto the visible path.
--title sets the tab title; rename without a title resets it.
split takes a direction (horizontal or vertical) and an optional command.
switch reveals the terminal and reports when a later navigation superseded it.
To start a fresh agent in the current worktree, create a terminal with --worktree active and the agent command.
A terminal created from the CLI in the background survives a window reload and is never revived later as a duplicate ghost tab.
split acts on exactly the terminal named even when its tab is parked in the background, without changing the active tab or taking focus.
acceptance: kolux terminal create --worktree active --command codex opens a Codex tab without stealing focus; adding --focus reveals it.
kolux terminal split --terminal h --direction vertical adds a side-by-side pane.
cards.compat: Commands terminal create|split|rename|switch, alias terminal focus; flags --worktree --command --title --focus --direction --terminal.

cards.title: kolux terminal close, with the old stop kept as a hidden alias
cards.user_does: Closes one terminal by handle, its whole tab, or every terminal in a worktree.
cards.user_sees: The terminal or terminals close; the result says whether each process was confirmed stopped.
rules: --tab closes the whole tab and waits until the change is saved durably.
--worktree with --all closes every terminal in that worktree.
Success is claimed only for a confirmed process kill; a process that may still be alive is reported as a failure (and fails --json).
A host too old for bulk close fails before changing anything.
terminal stop is deprecated and hidden; it points to close with --worktree and --all.
acceptance: kolux terminal close --worktree active --all closes all its panes and reports each confirmed.
kolux terminal stop is absent from help but still explains its replacement.
cards.compat: Command terminal close; flags --terminal --tab --worktree --all. Hidden: terminal stop.

cards.title: kolux automations list, show and runs
cards.user_does: Lists scheduled automations, shows one, or lists its past runs.
cards.user_sees: Each automation with its schedule, target and the host that owns it; runs show outcomes including skipped runs.
rules: Rows name the owning host; a row whose host is gone is shown as orphaned and explains why it cannot run.
Reading never needs the owning host to exist.
Automation ids can be given positionally or by flag.
acceptance: kolux automations list --json returns every automation shown in the Automations view.
kolux automations runs <id> lists a skipped run after a failing precheck.
cards.compat: Commands automations list|show|runs.

cards.title: kolux automations create, edit, remove and run
cards.user_does: Creates or edits a scheduled agent run with a name, schedule, prompt, provider and target; removes one; or runs one now.
cards.user_sees: The automation appears or changes in Kolux and runs on schedule; run starts it immediately.
rules: Schedule: hourly, daily, weekdays, weekly, a five-field cron line, or an RRULE; --schedule is an alias of --trigger; --time HH:MM, --day 0-6 with Sunday as 0, --timezone as an IANA name.
Schedule modifiers on edit need a schedule flag; invalid days are rejected before contacting the app.
Target: the current worktree by default; --repo or --workspace, never both; --workspace-mode existing or new-per-run (new worktree per run is the default).
--reuse-session sends later runs to the previous live session (existing-workspace only); --fresh-session is the opposite; both together are rejected.
--precheck runs a bounded command first; exit 0 continues, anything else records a skipped run; --precheck-timeout bounds it.
--enabled or --disabled; --missed-run-grace-minutes controls catching up a missed run.
--source-context takes JSON for task data; null on edit clears it; invalid JSON is rejected early.
Edits carry the owner they read; if another host now owns the automation the command explains the conflict and the recovery, without offering a retry for a removed target.
acceptance: kolux automations create --name r --trigger daily --time 09:00 --prompt review --provider claude creates a daily 9:00 automation in the current repo.
Precheck exiting 1 records a skipped run.
edit --day 7 is rejected without contacting the app.
cards.compat: Commands automations create|edit|remove|run; flags --name --trigger/--schedule --time --day --timezone --prompt --provider --repo --workspace --workspace-mode --reuse-session --fresh-session --precheck --precheck-timeout --enabled --disabled --missed-run-grace-minutes --source-context.

cards.title: Orchestration runs: create, bind, inspect
cards.user_does: A coordinator agent (or the user) starts an orchestration run with an objective, binds the current terminal to an existing run, checks which run is bound, lists runs or shows one.
cards.user_sees: A run record owned by the calling coordinator terminal; later orchestration commands from that terminal default to it.
rules: run-create binds the run to the resolved coordinator terminal.
run-use binds an existing run; --takeover-legacy adopts a legacy run and must be run in the live coordinator terminal it binds, keeping existing workers.
run-list is paginated by default with opaque cursors; run-show takes a run id.
Mutating run commands accept --retry-request for exact recovery.
run-current shows the run bound to the calling coordinator terminal (or to --from).
acceptance: kolux orchestration run-create --objective x then run-current in the same terminal shows that run.
kolux orchestration run-list --limit 1 returns one row and a cursor.
cards.compat: Commands orchestration run-create|run-use|run-current|run-list|run-show; flags --objective --id --from --takeover-legacy --limit --cursor --retry-request.

cards.title: Orchestration messages: send and reply
cards.user_does: An agent sends a typed message to a run mailbox, a dispatch, a terminal or a group, or replies to a question by message id.
cards.user_sees: A receipt naming who received it, any recipients that were skipped, and any delivery limits.
rules: Message types: status, dispatch, worker_done, merge_ready, escalation, handoff, decision_gate, question, heartbeat.
worker_done needs --outcome succeeded or failed; worker_done and heartbeat target one exact dispatch and cannot go to groups.
From inside an active dispatch an omitted recipient means the run's mailbox; --to dispatch:<id> sends attempt-specific guidance.
Group addresses are @all and @worktree:<id>.
Structured payload flags (--task-id, --dispatch-id, --files-modified, --report-path, --phase) are preferred over raw --payload JSON; mixing the two is rejected.
Multi-line bodies are delivered unchanged (use kolux.exe on Windows).
The sender is taken from the terminal's own handle and pane key in the environment; failing to resolve it is reported plainly.
reply takes --id and --body and must be run with the same kolux executable that asked.
acceptance: A worker sends worker_done with --outcome succeeded and no --to: the coordinator's run mailbox receives it.
send --type heartbeat --to @all is rejected before resolving the sender.
cards.compat: Commands orchestration send|reply; flags --to --run --from --subject --body --type --priority --thread-id --payload --task-id --dispatch-id --dispatch-capability --outcome --files-modified --report-path --phase --retry-request --id. Address forms run:, dispatch:, @all, @worktree:.

cards.title: Orchestration inbox: check and inbox
cards.user_does: An agent checks its mailbox once, peeks, acknowledges, or blocks waiting for new messages; or opens the inbox view of a terminal.
cards.user_sees: The oldest unacknowledged batch of messages in arrival order, with reply guidance for current rows.
rules: By default check returns the oldest unacknowledged batch; --ack acknowledges the previous batch first; --peek returns unread without marking read; --all returns everything without marking read; read modes cannot be combined.
--wait blocks until a matching message or --timeout-ms; while waiting it writes a keepalive line to stderr about every 15 seconds.
--types is only the wake condition; the returned batch is always whole.
--format renders rows as local text only and never writes into another terminal.
Rows from legacy runs are labelled and keep their bodies.
Older runtimes without peek are handled: already-read rows are filtered, a full 100-row page warns, and peek with wait fails clearly.
inbox --full includes all supported issue context within limits.
acceptance: Two messages arrive: check returns both; check --ack returns nothing new.
check --wait --timeout-ms 30000 prints keepalives on stderr and returns as soon as a message lands.
cards.compat: Commands orchestration check|inbox; flags --terminal --run --ack --unread --peek --all --types --format --wait --timeout-ms --limit --full --retry-request.

cards.title: Orchestration ask: a blocking question with resume
cards.user_does: A worker asks a coordinator or human a question (optionally with choices) and waits for the answer.
cards.user_sees: The answer when it arrives; on timeout, the pending message id and the exact command to resume waiting.
rules: --timeout-ms sets both the server wait and the client timeout; an omitted timeout leaves default headroom.
--resume continues waiting on an existing question without creating a new one; mixing create and resume input is rejected.
On packaged Windows the legacy protocol hands back with exit 75 so the caller can resume; resuming never hands back again.
--json output uses the shared envelope.
acceptance: Ask with a short timeout: the output includes a resume command that, when run, returns the later answer.
Ask with an invalid timeout is rejected before contacting the app.
cards.compat: Command orchestration ask; flags --to --run --question --resume --dispatch-capability --options --timeout-ms --from --retry-request. Exit 75 on Windows hand-off.

cards.title: Orchestration tasks and dispatch
cards.user_does: A coordinator creates tasks with dependencies, lists and updates them, dispatches a task to a worker terminal, and previews the dispatch preamble.
cards.user_sees: Task rows with status and readiness; dispatch results naming the worker; previews of the text a worker will receive.
rules: task-create takes a spec, short title, display name, dependencies and parent; the creator is the caller's terminal, re-derived from its pane key if the handle went stale, otherwise it fails closed.
Dependencies whose quotes PowerShell stripped are still passed through correctly.
task-list filters by status or readiness; --brief collapses whitespace and caps each spec at 160 characters, computed on the server or locally for older runtimes.
task-update sets status and result.
dispatch sends a task to a worker; --dry-run needs no recipient and returns only the preamble; --return-preamble includes it; --inject delivers into the terminal.
Dispatch refusals come back as clear errors through the normal error output.
dispatch-show shows a dispatch or its preamble.
acceptance: Create task B depending on A: task-list --ready excludes B until A is done.
dispatch --task t --dry-run prints the preamble and changes nothing.
cards.compat: Commands orchestration task-create|task-list|task-update|dispatch|dispatch-show; flags --spec --task-title --display-name --deps --parent --status --ready --brief --result --task --to --inject --dry-run --return-preamble --preamble --run --from --retry-request.

cards.title: Orchestration worker-start: launch a worker with model routing
cards.user_does: A coordinator starts a worker for a task (new or existing), in a new or existing worktree, optionally choosing agent, model, effort or a routing tier.
cards.user_sees: A receipt saying the worker is ready, failed or unknown, which mode actually ran, any partial effects left behind, and exact recovery commands.
rules: --task names an existing task; --spec creates one atomically.
--model accepts Claude, Codex and Cursor model ids; --effort needs --model; neither applies when reusing an existing --terminal.
--tier major, deep, build or light picks model and effort from the per-provider routing in Settings.
--on chooses only which server hosts the worker; the run stays where it is.
--retry-of needs --task and does not inherit placement.
Failed and unknown receipts exit nonzero; a live background worker gets a reveal hint; a structured chat refusal names the recovery.
If the runtime would drop the launch preferences, the command fails before starting.
acceptance: worker-start --spec x --tier build starts a worker on the model set for build and prints a ready receipt.
worker-start --effort high without --model is rejected.
cards.compat: Command orchestration worker-start; flags --task --spec --task-title --deps --parent --on --worktree --name --repo --base-branch --display-name --comment --setup --agent --model --effort --terminal --tier --retry-of --timeout-ms --run --from --retry-request.

cards.title: Orchestration workers: list, show, read, stop, abandon, release, retain
cards.user_does: A coordinator lists its workers, inspects one, reads its transcript, or ends, abandons, releases or keeps a worker.
cards.user_sees: Worker rows with state and the literal next command to run; transcripts with provenance; whether a worker is waiting on a person.
rules: worker-list defaults to the run bound to the calling terminal; --run overrides; with no bound run it lists every run; the scope is named in the output.
worker-list filters by terminal state, can include remote workers, pages with opaque cursors, limit 1 to 100; partial host failures are shown beside the rows.
worker-show can wait interactively; it says none only when the pane was checked and nothing was waiting, unknown otherwise.

worker-read pages a transcript with opaque cursors, labels terminal fallback evidence, distinguishes released archives from live ones, and separates the terminal process verdict from the agent verdict.
worker-stop warns when the process is kept; release and retain manage the worktree after completion.
Cleanup and retention timers are not exposed on the CLI.
Not every worker has a terminal: terminal commands refuse such a worker's handle, while worker-read with --source transcript always works; help states this limit without naming worker kinds.
acceptance: From a coordinator terminal, worker-list shows only that run's workers.
worker-read on a released worker says it is reading an archive.
cards.compat: Commands orchestration worker-list|worker-show|worker-read|worker-stop|worker-abandon|worker-release|worker-retain; flags --dispatch --source --cursor --limit --run --terminal-state --include-remote --retry-request.

cards.title: Orchestration decision gates
cards.user_does: A coordinator opens a gate that waits for a decision, resolves it, or lists gates.
cards.user_sees: Gate rows and their resolution.
rules: gate-create uses the bound coordinator handle and fails with an actionable error, changing nothing, when no run is bound.
An explicit --from is accepted without checking terminal liveness.
gate-list is scoped to the caller's run, or inspects a named run without binding.
gate-resolve takes the gate --id and a --resolution, optionally --from, and accepts --retry-request.
acceptance: gate-create from an unbound terminal fails without creating anything.
cards.compat: Commands orchestration gate-create|gate-resolve|gate-list.

cards.title: Safe retry after an unknown result: --retry-request, request-show, reset
cards.user_does: Re-runs an orchestration change whose outcome was lost (dropped connection), looks up a request's state, or resets orchestration state.
cards.user_sees: The retried change applies at most once; request-show states what happened to a request; reset clears the chosen scope.
rules: Only orchestration changes carry a durable request id; when the connection drops the error prints the exact command to retry with --retry-request.
--retry-request must be a UUID and is only for exact recovery.
An older local runtime is refused before any orchestration change is sent.
request-show asks without sending a change and gives an honest reading of the state; it names the version gap on older servers.
reset needs exactly one scope (--all, --tasks or --messages); a bare reset is rejected before contacting the app.
request-show takes the request id with --request.
acceptance: Drop the connection mid task-create: the error shows a retry command; running it creates exactly one task.
kolux orchestration reset alone is rejected.
cards.compat: Flag --retry-request <uuid> on orchestration mutations and terminal send; commands orchestration request-show and reset (--all|--tasks|--messages).

cards.title: Who is calling: orchestration caller identity
cards.user_does: Runs orchestration commands from an agent terminal, a structured chat session or an outside shell.
cards.user_sees: Commands act as the terminal they run in; impersonation and stale identities are refused with a clear reason.
rules: Identity comes from the terminal's handle and pane key in the environment; --from names a handle explicitly where allowed.
A stale handle is re-derived from the pane key; if that cannot be proven the command fails closed.
A structured worker can run orchestration commands as itself; a chat session with no orchestration identity is refused.
Legacy runs are read-only from the CLI; legacy worker settlements are accepted only when attested, never from an unattested relay.
Lifecycle verdicts the runtime rejects are reported as failures, including in --json.

A worker_done send whose dispatch cannot be shown to settle (for example the dispatch had already failed for another reason and left its task blocked) is reported as an unknown outcome and fails, never as success.
acceptance: Running check from a plain shell without a handle fails with a clear identity error.
A worker's worker_done from a different pane does not complete the task.
cards.compat: Environment variables KOLUX_TERMINAL_HANDLE and KOLUX_PANE_KEY; flag --from.

cards.title: kolux agent hooks: status, on, off, prepare-codex
cards.user_does: Checks whether agent status hooks are installed, turns them on or off, or prepares Codex's trusted hook setup.
cards.user_sees: Hook state per agent, and confirmation of the change.
rules: prepare-codex applies Codex trust using the current hooks setting and honours a Codex-specific disable even when the app is unreachable.
Uses the active profile's settings, not stale legacy ones, and respects a disable that has not finished saving.
Writing settings while offline never switches on optional UI styles the user did not choose.
acceptance: kolux agent hooks off then status reports off; Claude panes stop reporting live status.
With Codex hooks disabled, prepare-codex leaves them disabled.
cards.compat: Commands agent hooks status|on|off|prepare-codex.

cards.title: kolux diagnostics memory
cards.user_does: Runs kolux diagnostics memory.
cards.user_sees: The same memory breakdown as the in-app resource usage popover, including committed memory beside resident memory.
rules: --json passes the committed figure through unchanged.
acceptance: Numbers match the Resource Usage popover taken at the same moment.
cards.compat: Command diagnostics memory.

cards.title: kolux agent-context: machine-readable map of every command
cards.user_does: An agent runs kolux agent-context --json to learn the CLI.
cards.user_sees: A versioned document listing every command with its path, aliases, argument mode, summary, usage, accepted flags (including the global ones), positional arguments, examples and notes. Without --json it prints only the command count and how to get the full schema.
rules: Answered from the CLI's own registry with the app closed; remote-target flags are ignored.
Commands are listed in a stable order; optional lists default to empty.
Raw passthrough commands are marked as such and get no synthesized Kolux flags.
Browser page targeting is not advertised on local discovery.
acceptance: kolux agent-context --json parses, its command count equals the number of entries, and worktree rm shows remove and delete as aliases.
cards.compat: Schema fields: schemaVersion (1), commandCount, commands[{command, path, aliases, argumentMode parsed|passthrough, summary, usage, flags, positionalArgs, examples, notes}].

cards.title: kolux skills list and get: bundled agent guides
cards.user_does: Lists the skill guides bundled with this CLI version, or prints one compactly, in full, or one of its references.
cards.user_sees: Topic names with one-line descriptions; the guide's Markdown.
rules: Works locally with the app closed; topics are listed in a stable order.
get prints the compact guide; --full the whole package; --references lists reference names; --reference prints one reference alone (also accepted as references/<file>.md or via a topic alias).
--full, --reference and --references cannot be combined; --reference on a topic without references or with an unknown name lists what exists.
Unknown topic exits nonzero and lists all topics.
skills show is an alias of get; --json gives canonical name, selection and Markdown with a stable shape.
The topic can be given positionally or with --topic.
acceptance: kolux skills get orchestration prints the compact guide; --full prints more.
kolux skills get nope exits nonzero listing valid topics.
cards.compat: Commands skills list|get (alias show); flags --full --reference --references --json.

cards.title: kolux skills install and update
cards.user_does: Installs or updates Kolux skills into the detected coding agents, globally or for the current project, or previews the command first.
cards.user_sees: The package command it is about to run (on stderr), then that tool's output; --dry-run prints the command without running it.
rules: With no --skill and no --all it lists what can be installed or updated; --skill repeats and accepts aliases; --all with --skill is rejected; unknown names are rejected.
--agent takes a comma list; by default it targets the agents Kolux detects and refuses to run when none is detected rather than targeting all.
--local installs for the project instead of globally.
--json only for --dry-run or listing; real runs reject --json.
The package tool's exit code is forwarded; a launch failure exits nonzero.
On Windows a .cmd package shim runs through cmd safely; paths that cmd would misread are reported; the current folder is never put on the tool's PATH.
Refuses to run when the shell forwards kolux to another machine's Kolux.
A package tool installed under a folder whose name has spaces or parentheses (such as the 32-bit Program Files folder) is run, not refused; a tool that is not a .cmd shim is started directly.
acceptance: kolux skills install --skill kolux-cli --dry-run prints the exact command and changes nothing.
With no agents detected, install without --agent refuses.
cards.compat: Commands skills install|update; flags --skill (repeatable) --all --agent --local --dry-run.

cards.title: Browser tabs and profiles (kolux tab ...)
cards.user_does: Lists, shows, creates, switches or closes Kolux browser tabs, and manages the browser profiles tabs use.
cards.user_sees: Tab rows with page ids and profile labels; new tabs open in the worktree's browser.
rules: Page ids from tab list are the reliable way to target a tab with --page; commands without --page act on the active tab of the worktree.
Current worktree is resolved only when --page is combined with --worktree current.
tab switch reveals only with --focus.
Profiles: list, create (isolated by default, imported scope or native user agent on request; unknown scope rejected), delete, set, show, use-default, clone a tab into another profile.
Browser commands are not offered on groups that are not about the browser.
Browser commands are top-level words (tab, snapshot, click, cookie, storage and so on), not under a browser group.
tab switch and tab close take a tab --index or a --page id; tab list --show-profile adds each tab profile.
Profile delete is marked destructive.
acceptance: kolux tab create --url x then tab list --json shows the new page id.
kolux tab profile create --label x --scope bogus is rejected.
cards.compat: Commands tab list|show|current|switch|create|close and tab profile list|create|delete|set|show|use-default|clone; flags --page --index --worktree --profile --label --scope --no-ua-spoof --show-profile --focus.

cards.title: Browser page interaction by snapshot references (kolux snapshot, click, fill ...)
cards.user_does: An agent navigates a browser tab, takes an accessibility snapshot, and clicks, types or fills elements by the references the snapshot gave.
cards.user_sees: Each action's result; snapshots list elements with short references (e1, e2 and so on).
rules: Workflow: open or navigate, snapshot, act on references, snapshot again after any navigation.
Navigation: goto, back, forward, reload.
Actions: click, dblclick, hover, drag, fill, type, inserttext, clear, select, select-all, check, uncheck, focus, keypress, scroll, scrollintoview, upload, mouse move/down/up/wheel.
Queries: get, is, find, highlight, eval.
wait accepts a selector or condition; selector waits get their own timeout budget, extended by --timeout.
exec passes a raw agent-browser command string through for anything without its own verb.
Every browser verb accepts --worktree to pick whose browser to drive.

Flags: type --input; scroll --direction up, down, left or right with --amount in pixels; eval --expression; wait --selector, --text, --url, --load, --fn, --state, --timeout; get and is --what; find --locator with --action, --value, --text; download --selector --path; highlight --selector; mouse move --x --y; mouse down and up --button; mouse wheel --dx --dy.
acceptance: Snapshot a login page, fill the email reference, click the submit reference: the page navigates.
browser wait with a selector that never appears times out without claiming Kolux is down.
cards.compat: Top-level words snapshot goto back forward reload click dblclick hover drag fill type inserttext clear select select-all check uncheck focus keypress scroll scrollintoview upload mouse get is find highlight eval wait exec; flags --element --value --worktree --page.

cards.title: Browser state, emulation and capture (kolux cookie, storage, set, screenshot ...)
cards.user_does: Reads or sets cookies and local or session storage, emulates a device, viewport, location, offline mode, headers, credentials or media type, intercepts or records network traffic, reads console and network logs, uses the clipboard, answers dialogs, downloads, or captures screenshots and PDFs.
cards.user_sees: The value read, a confirmation of the change, or the captured file.
rules: Empty values are kept for cookie value, storage value and credential password; empty names or keys and missing values are rejected before contacting the app.
Cookie expiry must be a finite non-negative number.
viewport has a mobile option; set device, offline, headers, credentials, media.
intercept enable, disable, list; capture start, stop; console; network.
clipboard read and write; dialog accept and dismiss; download.
screenshot, full-screenshot and pdf produce files; base64 sizes are reported decoded.
screenshot and full-screenshot take --format png or jpeg; cookie delete and storage clear are marked destructive.
geolocation overrides the page location with --latitude and --longitude, and optional --accuracy.

Flags: cookie set --name --value --domain --path --secure --httpOnly --sameSite --expires; cookie delete --name with --domain or --url; viewport --width --height --scale --mobile; set offline --state; set headers --headers; set credentials --user --pass; set media --color-scheme --reduced-motion; intercept enable --patterns.
acceptance: kolux storage local set --key a --value= stores an empty string.
kolux screenshot writes an image of the current tab.
cards.compat: Top-level words cookie get|set|delete, storage local|session get|set|clear, viewport, geolocation, set device|offline|headers|credentials|media, intercept enable|disable|list, capture start|stop, console, network, clipboard read|write, dialog accept|dismiss, download, screenshot, full-screenshot, pdf.

cards.title: Retired orchestration coordinator-start and coordinator-stop
cards.user_does: Runs orchestration coordinator-start or its alias orchestration run, or coordinator-stop or its alias run-stop.
cards.user_sees: A message that the command is retired and to load the current orchestration skill instead; nothing changes.
rules: The command has no runtime effect; it stays only to redirect old habits.
Already retired when the Kolux history begins (2026-09-10); the retirement predates the fork.
acceptance: n/a — decision item
cards.compat: Words orchestration coordinator-start|coordinator-stop, aliases orchestration run|run-stop.
evidence: git:21231c88b (first commit 2026-09-10) already carries the retired summary

cards.title: kolux serve: headless server
cards.user_does: Runs kolux serve to start Kolux without a window, optionally with pairing or recipe output.
cards.user_sees: A foreground headless server that remote clients can pair with.
rules: Contradictory pairing flags and bad ports are rejected before launch; it always runs locally.
acceptance: n/a — dropped
cards.decision: default cut: headless serve and web client are area 18. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Remote targeting: pairing codes, environments, hosts and paired-client URL opening
cards.user_does: Targets another Kolux with --pairing-code, --environment, KOLUX_PAIRING_CODE or KOLUX_ENVIRONMENT, manages saved environments, lists hosts, uses --host runtime:<id>, or opens a URL on the paired client.
cards.user_sees: Commands run against the chosen remote Kolux; environment and host lists show what can be targeted.
rules: Local-only groups (account, environment, host, serve, agent, vm, agent-context) ignore remote selection; host list rejects explicit remote flags.
An explicit --host runtime:<id> outranks ambient pairing settings; disagreements are refused.
KOLUX_CLI_CWD lets the SSH relay pass the remote caller's folder.
open-url opens a link on the paired client hosting the terminal.
acceptance: n/a — dropped
cards.decision: default cut: saved environments, pairing codes, SSH hosts and paired clients are area 18. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: kolux project host setups
cards.user_does: Lists, creates, updates or deletes project host setups, or makes a project available on a host by importing a folder or cloning.
cards.user_sees: Host setup records per project.
rules: Relative paths are rejected for remote and SSH targets; --project with --host targets a setup on worktree create and automations.
acceptance: n/a — dropped
cards.decision: default cut: host setups (table 1b, per-repo pages). Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: kolux inside WSL distros
cards.user_does: Uses kolux from a WSL shell after Kolux registers a launcher in the distro.
cards.user_sees: kolux commands in WSL reach the Windows app.
rules: Registrations per distro are reconciled and serialized; Windows paths are translated to distro paths.
acceptance: n/a — dropped
cards.decision: default cut: WSL execution is area 18. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: kolux vm recipe doctor
cards.user_does: Checks or test-provisions an ephemeral VM recipe.
cards.user_sees: Recipe findings, or the full transcript when provisioning fails.
rules: Runs locally without the app; warns when no cleanup hook exists.
acceptance: n/a — dropped
cards.decision: default cut: ephemeral VM recipes are area 18. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: kolux emulator
cards.user_does: Drives the mobile emulator pane (gestures, logs and similar).
cards.user_sees: Emulator actions and output.
rules: Gesture points must be normalized coordinates.
acceptance: n/a — dropped
cards.decision: default cut: iOS/Android emulator pane is area 18. Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: kolux computer: desktop app control
cards.user_does: Lists apps and windows, reads app state, and clicks, types or presses keys in desktop apps.
cards.user_sees: Action results with screenshots and follow-up commands.
rules: Actions can target a window explicitly; permission setup is offered when missing.
acceptance: n/a — dropped
cards.decision: default cut: computer use (table 1b). Revive via DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: kolux linear and Linear issue links on worktrees
cards.user_does: Reads and edits Linear issues from the CLI, or links a Linear issue when creating or editing a worktree.
cards.user_sees: Linear issue data; the worktree shows the linked Linear issue.
rules: --linear-issue accepts an identifier or URL; null clears it on set; invalid values are rejected before contacting the app.
acceptance: n/a — dropped
